localChanges: The label is centred on its tile and wider than it, so at the edges of the layer canvas the overhang was clipped and, because that canvas is what the portal tiles, appeared nowhere at all (#49). On an 80x50 world at scale 2, `uMgungundlovu` on the first or last column lost 46 of its 124 pixels, and any name on the last row was drawn entirely below the canvas and was invisible.

`World.get` wraps both axes and `Portal.render()` tiles the canvas on both, so a label crossing an edge is now drawn a second time offset by the canvas width or height, which puts the overflow where the adjacent tiled copy shows it.

`4607766` set out to fix the last-row case by taking `(x * size) % canvas.width` for the offsets. That is a no-op — `x` is always below the world width, so the product is always below the canvas width — and the case was still broken.

While in here, `update()` now honours the tiles it is passed. It used to ignore them, clear the whole canvas and walk every tile in the world looking for cities, on every patch (#48). It keeps track of where each label was drawn instead, so it can clear just the boxes an update invalidated and redraw only the labels that overlapped them — a label overhangs its neighbours, so clearing one can bite into another. Measured over comparable windows of automated play, the layer went from seventeen full-canvas clears (4,915,200 pixels each) to 245,160 pixels cleared in total, and is now the least of the twelve layers rather than the only one clearing everything.

Verified in the browser against a real asset import: `Ulaanbaatar` and its size digit render correctly, no layer performs a full-canvas clear any more, and the wrap was confirmed by replicating the geometry and text metrics exactly — pixels now land at both edges for the first and last columns, and at the top for the last row, where before there were none.
